effort_rubric.1: Trivial, well-understood change. A few hours; no real unknowns.
effort_rubric.2: Small, self-contained task. About a day.
effort_rubric.3: Moderate task with a couple of moving parts. One to two days.
effort_rubric.5: Substantial task spanning a few components. Around half a week.
effort_rubric.8: Large task with real unknowns or cross-component coordination. About a week.
effort_rubric.13: Very large or highly uncertain — should probably be split into smaller tickets.

tone.title: Short imperative phrase, roughly 3-8 words, naming the outcome. E.g. 'Build file upload intake endpoint', 'Freeze core status vocabulary'. No trailing punctuation.
tone.description: One crisp sentence stating intent — what and why. No filler, no restating the title.
tone.acceptance_criteria: 1-4 concrete, testable, closeable conditions. Each independently checkable; phrase as the done-state, not a task. E.g. 'enforces max size with a clear error'.

1.name: Basic
1.requirements: Established implementation pattern; local change; straightforward verification.

2.name: Standard
2.requirements: Routine business logic, coordination across components, or a well-defined integration.

3.name: Complex
3.requirements: Complex state transitions, permissions, data migration, compatibility, or recovery behavior.

4.name: Advanced
4.requirements: Architecture tradeoffs, concurrency correctness, demanding performance, or complex security requirements.

guidance: Standard hours = the active work a developer competent in the stack and familiar with the project needs to meet the acceptance criteria: implementation, testing, self-review and handoff. Exclude waiting for dependencies or review, and person-specific onboarding.
Support every estimate with the breakdown (implementation + testing + self-review + handoff), in quarter-hour increments. Quarter hours standardise inputs; they are not a promise of that accuracy.

Pick the best-matching difficulty level from technical evidence and give a short task-specific reason. File count, code volume and repetitive work affect hours, not difficulty; never raise difficulty just because a task is long, and never pad the hours as a second complexity buffer.
A routine task involving authentication does not automatically qualify for level 4.
Record confidence separately: high when scope and approach are established, medium when bounded assumptions remain, low when material questions are unresolved. Confidence never changes points.
If a task can't be estimated responsibly, leave it Unestimated and flag needs_clarification; substantial unknowns may need a bounded investigation task first.
Estimate the work, not the person: assignment, individual speed, seniority and team size are never inputs. The same task gets the same points whoever takes it.

Ordinary testing and self-review stay inside a task's estimate. Substantial cleanup, integration or client preparation can be its own task (work_kind). Fixing your own incomplete work does not create additional points.
When scope changes, re-estimate with a reason; earlier estimates are kept in the task's history.

A full takeover is a reassignment. Partial work handed over becomes a separately owned 'replaced' split: the original keeps only what its owner did, and the original plus all its splits never total more than the original estimate unless the growth was approved.
Work completed before a switch to hours-based points stays on its legacy points with the owner recorded at the switch; it is never re-estimated, and new work goes in a new task.
